title: Louis's musical directors and rehearsing for TV
summary: Armstrong rarely rehearsed bands himself; Billy Kyle and earlier Joe Garland and Louis Russell handled it.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I was going to ask you -- in 1930 --
(Inaudible) when you saw Louis in Washington, whom was he working with? Did you have a group or -- would he appear in front of a local group?

I think Louie was playing in front of Louis Russell's group, Louis Russell's group, at that time. Of course, Louie had a lot of bands of his own back at that time, but if I'm not -- I'm not sure, but I'm pretty -- I think he was fronting Louis Russell's band at that time. You see, Louis never did rehearse bands much himself. He always had a musical director, somebody in the band who was an arranger to do this for him.
I know once with his big band he had Joe Garland, the saxophone player, the guy who wrote In the Mood. He had
Joe Garland to conduct his band, and Louis -- Lou Russell used to be his musical director. Even with the little band I had when I was with him, he had -- he used Billy Kyle as a musical director.

For instance, if we went in a town and Louie had to rehearse for a TV show or something, well, Billy was -- Louie didn't have to go out, but Louie could go home and relax. Billy would go and tell them what songs Louie was doing, and most of the stars do it that way, you know, and they don't fool around there all day doing that.

But we would go, and Billy Kyle would instruct them on just what key Louis did this or that in, and how many choruses, this and that, how he went out, and Billy Kyle would probably write out a little sketch for him and give it to him on just what we were doing, you know.

And we would rehearse. Sometimes Louis would rehearse with us, if it was something very important, but usually he went to the hotel, and he relaxed, you know. And most of them do -- that's the way they do it today, you know.

I know when Nat Cole had his group going, he used Lee Young a lot of times to do that for him, when Lee Young was playing with his group. But with Louie it was -- it just was one big thing after another, because you never knew when he had -- he had all these big things coming up. If we weren't doing a movie. We were doing a big TV show or something of
this sort, and, of course, he never was on real long, but he always had an important spot in these things to do, you know.
